subject: watching an agent run in a real Factorio client: what actually blocked it
conclusion: A connected client never broke the RCON transport. RCONClient.command treated the arrival of its sentinel's reply as proof the real reply was complete, which holds only on a server with no players. With a client attached the order inverts for anything longer than a trivial command, so the sentinel was read as an empty response and the real reply was discarded as stale on the next call -- one lost reply per call, indefinitely, surfacing as 'non-json rcon response'. Completion is now 'both replies seen', in either order.

lead_a_what_the_logs_said.note: This was the biggest gap: the log that had been read was runtime/workers/<id>/engine.log, which --console-log fills with console output only. The engine's real log is write-data/factorio-current.log and nobody had opened it.
lead_a_what_the_logs_said.full_engine_log_during_the_failure: no error, no warning: 'Serving map(...\temp\mp-save-0.zip) for peer(1) size(633363) crc(1454488875)' / 'processed PlayerJoinGame peerID(1) playerIndex(0) mode(create)' / 'received stateChanged peerID(1) ... newState(InGame)'
console_log_during_the_failure: [COMMAND] <server> (command): local ok, result = pcall(function() return remote.call("frrl_bridge", "run", "return 1") end) ...
lead_a_what_the_logs_said.reading: Two sentinels precede the command they were meant to follow, and the third request's command is not logged before its sentinel at all. The commands execute; the replies are simply not in the order the reader assumed.

reply_size.method: rcon.print(string.rep('x', N)) over a raw socket, packets counted
reply_size.with_client: 100, 1000, 4000, 4096, 8000, 16000, 32000, 64000 all returned size+1 bytes in exactly 1 packet
reply_size.consequence: this build never splits an RCON reply, so multi-packet fragmentation cannot be the failure and the 4096-byte Source RCON split is unused

command_size.method: padded /c command, 53 to 15993 bytes, side-effecting counter to prove execution
command_size.consequence: a 16 KB command survives a connected client; the 10 KB scenario_define was never too big

the_pause.method: reproduce the failure with configure(free_running=true) and tick_paused read back
the_pause.measured: applied {'free_running': True}, 'tick_paused after setup: False', client InGame, then session.reset raised 'transport failure: non-json rcon response'
the_pause.consequence: confirms the earlier session's finding: the pause was not the cause

server_side_screenshots.method: graphical binary with --start-server, game.take_screenshot at 640x640 and 320x320, script-output polled 15 s while ticks advanced (updateTick reached 952)
server_side_screenshots.measured: take_screenshot is a 'function', the call returns, script-output stays empty
server_side_screenshots.consequence: --start-server puts the full binary in headless mode, so there is no renderer. Confirms src/factoriorl/capture.py, and now names the reason.

graphical_host_with_rcon.rcon: absent: the 94-line log contains no 'RemoteCommandProcessor.cpp:126: Starting RCON interface' (the --start-server log has it at 0.532), and connecting gives WinError 10061 'actively refused'
graphical_host_with_rcon.also: --host ignores --bind (hosts at 0.0.0.0:0) and stops at an 'enter player name' dialog unless write-data/player-data.json carries a service-username
graphical_host_with_rcon.consequence: one graphical process that both renders and answers RCON is not available on this build; the working shape is headless server + graphical client

the_fix.change: RCONClient.command completes on 'seen a packet for the request id AND a packet for the sentinel id', in either order, instead of on the sentinel alone. Every command gets at least one packet bearing its id -- an empty-bodied one when it printed nothing -- so this is a property of the connection rather than another timing assumption.
the_fix.instrumentation: RCONClient.reordered_replies counts inversions; 0 on every player-free run, 15 across a six-step probe with a client attached
the_fix.silent_commands: Lua now goes out as /silent-command by default. Factorio broadcasts a /c command verbatim to every connected player, and each command here is a page of pcall/remote.call wrapper, so a watched run was unreadable behind its own command text. Measured: /sc rcon.print('sc-ok') answered with 6 bytes and appeared in neither the console log nor a player's chat, while the five /c probes alongside it were all logged. FACTORIO_RL_ECHO_COMMANDS=1 restores /c and with it the engine-side record.

exact_stepping_with_a_client_attached.method: plate_line scene installed, client joined, no free_running, six session.step({'action': 'wait'}, ticks=30) with game.tick and game.tick_paused read back between each
exact_stepping_with_a_client_attached.consequence: the measured contract survives being watched. tools/watch_agent.py still defaults to free running, because a world that freezes for the seconds an inference takes is a poor thing to watch -- that is now a preference, not a workaround, and --exact-stepping is available.

what_a_watched_run_still_perturbs: Joining creates a LuaPlayer no measured run has, and the default free-running mode lands each action at whatever tick it arrives at. Both are recorded in the run manifest; nothing produced by tools/watch_agent.py belongs in docs/evidence.
